title: BitGo Qualified Custody Accounts: What's the Difference?
summary: Keeping crypto secure is one thing. Using, trading, or holding cash alongside it without pulling it from a vault is another. BitGo lets you do both from insured, qualified custody.
body_markdown:
Keeping your crypto secure is one thing. Actually using it, trading it, or holding cash alongside it, without pulling it out of a vault every time, is another. BitGo gives you ways to do both from insured, qualified custody.


Go Accounts and Custody Wallets are backed by the same[qualified custody](https://www.bitgo.com/resources/blog/qualified-custody-vs-self-custody/) protections that BitGo provides for billions in institutional capital: multi-signature/MPC key security, segregated bankruptcy-remote accounts, insurance coverage of up to $250 million (subject to policy terms), and a federally regulated custodian, backed by a publicly traded parent company, legally responsible for keeping your assets safe.


## Qualified Custody provides strong protection


BitGo has two types of Qualified Custody: Go Accounts and segregated Custody Wallets. Before getting into how they differ, it helps to know how much they share. Both are qualified custody, and both get the same core protections underneath:


-


Both are held by BitGo Bank & Trust, a regulated trust bank with a legal duty to protect your assets, not just software you use yourself.


-


Both keep keys in cold-storage, locked away in physical, offline vaults.


-


Both are[insured](https://www.bitgo.com/solutions/insurance/) up to $250 million against loss, theft, or misuse.


-


Both let you set up your own rules, like spending limits or an approved list of addresses, if you want extra control.


-


Both offer live video ID checks, so a real person is verified before money moves, as an added layer of security.


In other words, choosing between them isn't about which one is safer. It's about which one fits how you plan to use your money.


## How are the keys stored?


Whether it's a Go Account or a segregated Custody Wallet, BitGo’s custody wallets are secured by three keys, and BitGo manages all three on your behalf. The user key, which authorizes your intent to move funds, is normally something a self-custody client would hold themselves, but in custody, BitGo holds it for you instead. The BitGo key acts as the policy enforcer and co-signer on every transaction, and it's always protected by dedicated and audited secure hardware, regardless of whether you're in self-custody or custody. The backup key exists purely for disaster recovery, and just like the user key, it shifts from client-held in self-custody to BitGo-managed in custody.


In short, both wallet types are qualified custody, meaning that the keys are secured and managed by BitGo - an established custodian in digital assets for over a decade.

## Go Account Custody vs Segregated Custody Wallets


### Segregated Qualified Custody Wallets


Think of a segregated Custody Wallet as a safe deposit box for the long haul. Your bitcoin or other digital assets sit in cold storage, offline and locked down, with the highest level of security BitGo offers. The tradeoff is speed: moving funds out can take up to 24 hours, since it's built for safety over convenience.


### Go Account: Your Default Qualified Custody Account


Go Accounts are built for using your assets, not just storing them. You can hold cash and digital assets together in one place, trade directly, access liquidity, and put assets to work, all without moving them out of qualified custody. Deposits show up within minutes, and withdrawals typically clear in a few hours instead of a full day.


When you move funds within a Go Account, BitGo simply updates its internal ledger, the same way a bank updates your account when you move money between your checking and savings accounts. Nothing has to hit the blockchain, so it happens almost instantly and your assets stay just as protected the whole time. Sending money to a wallet outside BitGo from a Go Account still requires a blockchain transaction, so it will take a bit longer.

## Which wallet do you need?


With both giving the benefits of qualified custody, it can be a pretty simple decision. Use a Custody Wallet for savings you don't plan to touch often. Use a Go Account for the crypto and cash you're actively managing. Most people end up using both: one for holding, one for trading and transactions.
